LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Living Together Suggested vocabulary share, respect, together, love, care, livin
Topic 12.1: Listening and speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Living Together Suggested vocabulary share, respect, together, love, care, livin in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How would you know if someone is listening to you? 2. How do we learn to pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn-is enhanced as they collaboratively practise using vocabulary learnt to express own ideas.

Values:
Respect-Patience is enhanced as the learner accepts diverse opinions from others in group activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship-Social cohesion is enhanced as the learner practices living together in harmony.

Link to other Learning Areas

Attentive listening and knowledge of vocabulary will help learners in all learning areas.

Audio recordings, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,
